title: Makkah opened
hook: He came back to the city that drove him out, at the head of ten thousand, and took no revenge.

screens.text: **He came back to the city that drove him out.** Eight and a half years earlier he had left it at night, hunted. Now he returned at the head of ten thousand. Everyone waited to see what he would do.
**A broken truce.** Quraysh's allies broke the truce of Hudaybiyah, IslamQA reports [IslamQA 11575]. So in Ramadan, 8 AH, the Prophet ﷺ set out for Makkah with ten thousand people [Bukhari 4276].
bubbles: We tell the history, not the fighting. His rule held: no harming women or children [Bukhari 3015].

screens.prompt: You're in Makkah that day. The man your city mocked, starved and drove out now has ten thousand behind him. What do you expect?

options.text: Safety offered, and old enemies forgiven
options.feedback: That's what happened. He entered almost without fighting, offered safety, and forgave people who had hurt him deeply.

options.text: Revenge on everyone who hurt him
options.feedback: That's what many expected. Instead he took no revenge for himself [Bukhari 3560].

options.text: The city burned to the ground
options.feedback: Not quite. He entered almost without fighting and announced who would be safe [Muslim 1780].

screens.text: **Safety in an old enemy's house.** Abu Sufyan had led Quraysh against him for years and had just accepted Islam [Yaqeen, Confronting Hate]. The Prophet ﷺ announced: whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe [Muslim 1780].
bubbles: The Ansar, the Madinans who had taken him in, feared he'd now stay in Makkah. He said he'd live and die among them, and they wept [Muslim 1780].

screens.text: Eight and a half years after he left.

screens.text: **Truth has come.** He entered Makkah almost without fighting and went to the Ka'bah, the House built for Allah alone. Around it stood 360 idols. He struck them down with a stick, reciting: *"Truth has come, and falsehood has departed"* [Bukhari 4287; Q 17:81, Saheeh Intl.].

options.feedback: Yes. He recited it as the idols around the Ka'bah came down [Bukhari 4287].
Not quite. Falsehood has departed: the verse he recited at the Ka'bah [Q 17:81].
Not quite. Falsehood has departed. The idols didn't hide; they came down [Bukhari 4287].

screens.text: **Power is tested by mercy.** He forgave people who had hurt him deeply, Yaqeen reports: Hind, 'Ikrimah son of Abu Jahl, and Wahshi, who had killed his uncle Hamzah [Yaqeen, Confronting Hate; Bukhari 4072]. Day 15 said he took no revenge. This is how.
bubbles: Someone from your old life may have mocked your faith. When the day comes that they need you, mercy is still yours to choose.

screens.situation: Ana's older cousin mocked her hijab for months. Now he's lost his job and asks if he can sleep on her couch for a week. She's still hurt.

options.text: Help him, and if it feels right, tell him calmly how the mocking felt
options.feedback: Yes. Mercy without pretending it didn't hurt. That's the Makkah way.

options.text: Remind him of every insult and say no
options.feedback: Not quite. Her hurt is real, but payback isn't the Prophet's ﷺ way [Bukhari 3560].

options.text: Help only if he apologises in front of the whole family first
options.feedback: Not quite. He didn't demand public apologies from Makkah. Kindness first; honest talk can follow.

screens.text: He came home with ten thousand and the power to repay every wound. He chose safety and forgiveness. Power is tested by mercy.
Next episode: Hunayn. A valley ambush, and the people who'd given the most felt left out.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Quraysh's allies broke the Hudaybiyah truce [IslamQA 11575] (single text source; "IslamQA reports"). In Ramadan, 8 AH, eight and a half years after the hijra, he set out with ten thousand [Bukhari 4276].
- He announced that whoever entered Abu Sufyan's house would be safe [Muslim 1780]; Abu Sufyan, long an enemy, had just accepted Islam [Yaqeen, Confronting Hate].
- Some of the Ansar thought love of his city would keep him in Makkah; he told them he had migrated to Allah and to them, and would live and die with them; they wept [Muslim 1780, the long narration of 'Abdullah ibn Rabah from Abu Hurayrah].
- He entered almost without fighting, found 360 idols around the Ka'bah and struck them with a stick, reciting Q 17:81 [Bukhari 4287].
- He forgave old enemies, among them Hind, Wahshi and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl [Yaqeen, Confronting Hate] (single source; "Yaqeen reports"). Wahshi had killed Hamzah at Uhud and later became Muslim [Bukhari 4072].
- He never took revenge for himself [Bukhari 3560]; Day 15 already teaches "he took no revenge".

**Likely questions**
- *"Did he really say 'No blame on you today; go, you are free'?"* It's a well-known line from the early biographies, but its chain isn't confirmed as sound, so this track doesn't put it on screen. Say: "It's a well-known story whose chain scholars consider weak. What's certain is that he took no revenge [Bukhari 3560] and offered safety [Muslim 1780]." (scholar question Q43)
- *"Was there no fighting at all?"* Say "almost without fighting", as the sources do, and don't describe any clashes. His rule protecting women and children held [Bukhari 3015]. (scholar question Q39)
- *"Did he forgive Wahshi completely?"* Wahshi became Muslim and was not punished; the Prophet ﷺ asked him to keep out of his sight, the grief of a man who had lost his uncle [Bukhari 4072]. Present it honestly: forgiveness with human grief, not anger.
- *"Why were there idols at the Ka'bah?"* Over the centuries the Arabs added idol worship to Ibrahim's religion (seerah-01). The Ka'bah was built for Allah alone; Muslims don't worship it.
- *"How do I forgive someone who hurt me?"* Forgiveness doesn't erase boundaries or safety. Start with du'a, then small steps. If someone is abusive or dangerous, the safety rule comes first; don't advise reconnecting.

**Escalate:** abusive or unsafe family situations (safety rule); any question about fighting today (Day 71 frame and the imam).

**Don't**
- Don't quote "No blame on you today" as his words or put it on a screen. (scholar question Q43)
- Don't describe the clashes or Khalid's sector.
- Don't compare the convert's family or their faith to the idols of Makkah.
- Don't tell a convert they must reconcile with someone who is unsafe.

- [Bukhari 4072](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4072) (Sahih): Wahshi's account of Uhud and his later Islam.
- [Bukhari 3015](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3015) (Sahih): no killing of women or children.
- [Bukhari 2731](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2731) (Sahih): the truce of Hudaybiyah.
- [IslamQA 11575, *Who Is Muhammad?*](https://islamqa.info/en/answers/11575): the truce broken.
